structure: Independent persons sampled from a centered trivariate Gaussian population. The population covariance satisfies both records. Unreported correlations with measured Z are completed by an explicitly assumed, positive-definite scenario. Adjustment means separate population OLS regressions of X and Y on an intercept and Z.

parameter_provenance.basis: Exact population means in X, Y, Z order.
Covariance equals correlation because both variances are one.

requested_estimands.name: partial_xy_given_z
requested_estimands.basis: For a=Corr(X,Z) and b=Corr(Y,Z), the residual correlation is (0.5-a*b)/sqrt((1-a^2)*(1-b^2)). Records do not determine a or b. Choosing a=0.6 and b=0.5 gives the reported scenario value.

requested_estimands.name: marginal_xy
requested_estimands.basis: Record A directly specifies this population Pearson correlation, independently of the chosen joint distribution.

requested_estimands.name: slope_x_on_z
requested_estimands.basis: The population OLS slope with an intercept is Cov(X,Z)/Var(Z). Record C fixes Var(Z)=1, but the numerator is unreported and is chosen as 0.6.

limitations: The Z relationships and adjusted correlation are scenario choices, not identified evidence-composition results.
The records do not determine distributional shape or higher moments.
Population standardization does not imply exact realized sample means, variances, or correlations; the generator performs no sample calibration or selection.
These artificial associations provide no causal interpretation or biomedical validation.
